what: Website-fingerprinting resistance of the WireGuard + DAITA carrier, measured with tools/daita_lab.py and tools/wf_attack.py, and protocol identification with nDPI 4.2 (ndpiReader) and TShark 4.4.19

setup.chain: 2 hops in network namespaces (client, relay, exit, destination), constant cells on every hop
setup.latency: netem 10 ms (+-1 ms) at each end of every link: about 60 ms round trip end to end
setup.workload: 8 synthetic sites (main document plus 3-28 objects, 77-594 KB), 15 loads each in shuffled order, 2 parallel connections, sizes +-15% and ~10% of objects skipped per load, 5 s between loads
setup.attack: k-FP-style features plus CUMUL, 500-tree random forest, stratified 5-fold cross-validation; closed world, chance 0.125

views.carrier: client <-> first hop: WireGuard + DAITA, what the client's ISP sees
views.inner link: first hop <-> exit: QUIC with constant cells, no DAITA (the same loads, as a baseline)

windows.true end + 3 s: each load cut at its true end: the attacker is told where every page finished
windows.fixed 6 s: every load gets the same 6 s from its true start: the fairer view of a constant-rate stream

accuracy.measured_on: the camouflaged carrier (QUIC on UDP 443), ~60 ms RTT, 8 sites x 15 loads, chance 0.125
accuracy.reading: balanced does not stop the attacker; strong reduces it to the shortest site (whose trace ends inside the window), the rest at or near chance. Wrapping in the HTTP/3 cloak did not change these versus the pre-cloak measurement.

strong.rate: one 1380-byte packet every ~21 ms per direction, continuously while keepalives flow

defects found in v0.5.0: FRONT got its padding window as 1-4 microseconds (maybenot-machines takes microseconds; Tamaraw scales seconds itself): every decoy left at once, 1.1 ms apart, at the tunnel's first packet
FRONT ran once per tunnel: no decoys around any later page load, including after WireGuard rekeys

Upstream Tamaraw stopped counting packets once data flowed, so traces were never rounded (5 of 120 a multiple of 100); each ended with ~98 decoys sent 1 us apart, marking when the page finished, and one more decoy after the trace
The QUIC ClientHello between hops named the tool: SNI <role>.advanced-vpn.internal and ALPN advanced-vpn/1, readable by anyone on the path (QUIC Initial packets are decryptable)

protocol identification.carrier, now: nDPI 4.2: QUIC (proto 188), category Web — the WireGuard+DAITA carrier rides inside the HTTP/3 cloak on UDP 443, so it is not identified as a VPN (was: WireGuard, category VPN)
protocol identification.between hops: nDPI: QUIC, category Web, ALPN h3, no hostname
protocol identification.caveat: the outer QUIC is real but its handshake fingerprint (quinn transport parameters, TLS ClientHello) is not a mainstream browser's; a JA4-style QUIC fingerprinter can tell it is not Chrome, and the certificate is self-signed

padding.carrier data packets: every WireGuard data packet 1380 bytes on the wire (14,706 balanced, 29,565 strong); only handshakes (156/100) and empty keepalives (40) differ

http3_camouflage.what: advanced-vpn-cloak carries each WireGuard datagram as a QUIC DATAGRAM frame on UDP 443 (ALPN h3, no SNI unless a cover name is set, server key pinned by SPKI)
http3_camouflage.on_the_wire: managed_test.py confirms zero WireGuard messages on the client's physical link; only QUIC, with one padded outer packet size (quinn pad_to_mtu). The first hop answers an unauthenticated probe with an HTTP/3 404 and forwards nothing (src/cloak.rs tests).
http3_camouflage.fingerprinting_unchanged: wrapping does not change DAITA's protection: balanced website-fingerprinting accuracy is 0.625 over the camouflaged carrier (fixed 6 s window, 8 sites, chance 0.125), the same as before the cloak
http3_camouflage.fails_closed: the cloak needs an underlay IPv4 MTU >= 1448 (a 1420-byte QUIC UDP payload); below that the client refuses to connect and keeps the kill switch (whole-device: all traffic dropped; applications: no route). Proven at MTU 1440 (refused) vs 1448 (accepted) in tools/mtu_test.py-style runs.
http3_camouflage.roaming: changing the client's address mid-transfer is survived in both defenses (the cloak reconnects, the carrier keepalive re-learns the address); strong recovers more slowly as its shaping restarts

strong_mode_stall_fix.symptom: before the fix, if the first hop was unreachable while the client started in strong mode, DAITA's Tamaraw shaper could hold traffic and never resume once the path returned
strong_mode_stall_fix.cause: GotaTun fired maybenot PaddingSent for decoys that could not be sent (no session), permanently exhausting the cumulative max_decoy_frac budget, so decoys (the only delay-queue drain) stopped; the delay state then never ended
strong_mode_stall_fix.fix: vendor/gotatun: do not count a decoy that has no session to send on, and add a liveness guard that flushes the delay queue when real packets sit behind active blocking with no decoy drain for 3 s
strong_mode_stall_fix.proven: with the carrier watchdog disabled, strong mode self-recovers from 15 s and 40 s start outages (tools/daita_lab.py, OUTAGE mode); the avpnctl carrier watchdog remains as a backstop
